LESSON: COMPASS DIRECTION

Grade: Grade 4
Subject: SOCIAL STUDIES
Strand: Natural and Historic Built Environments Compass Direction (6 lessons) Location a
Topic 1.1: Compass Direction

SECTION 1: WELCOME

Hello! This is a study lesson on Compass Direction. Read the explanation, follow every worked example, then do the practice. This is original CBC Learn content written from KICD outcomes — not a copy of a commercial textbook.

Big question: How can we show direction of places?

SECTION 2: WHAT YOU WILL LEARN

By the end of this lesson, you will be able to:

1. identify the four cardinal points of a compass
2. use the four cardinal points to give directions on a map
3. appreciate the use of four cardinal points in everyday life

SECTION 3: STUDY NOTES (READ AND LEARN)

WHAT YOU ARE STUDYING: COMPASS DIRECTION
Subject: SOCIAL STUDIES · Grade: Grade 4
This is a learner study lesson (not a teacher guide). Read every part, follow the models, then practise.

BIG PICTURE
Compass Direction helps you succeed in SOCIAL STUDIES. You will understand it, practise it, and use it in your county, school, and Kenyan community.

KEY FACTS: COMPASS DIRECTION
Good citizens follow rules, respect others, and care for shared places.
Kenyan examples: lining up, keeping the compound clean, telling the truth, helping a classmate.
Rights come with responsibilities.

PART 1: Identify the four cardinal points of a compass

What this means
In this part you learn to identify the four cardinal points of a compass. You will use ideas from in your county, school, and Kenyan community.

How to learn it
1. Read the idea carefully: identify the four cardinal points of a compass.
2. Locate, explain, then act responsibly using a Kenyan example from your life.
3. Check yourself: Can you explain it without looking?

Model
Locate: Connect “Compass Direction” to a real place or group in Kenya (school, market, county office, home).

Your turn
Do one short practice that proves you can identify the four cardinal points of a compass. Write or say your answer clearly.

PART 2: Use the four cardinal points to give directions on a map

What this means
In this part you learn to use the four cardinal points to give directions on a map. You will use ideas from in your county, school, and Kenyan community.

How to learn it
1. Read the idea carefully: use the four cardinal points to give directions on a map.
2. Locate, explain, then act responsibly using a Kenyan example from your life.
3. Check yourself: Can you explain it without looking?

Model
Explain: Give one cause and one effect linked to Compass Direction.

Your turn
Do one short practice that proves you can use the four cardinal points to give directions on a map. Write or say your answer clearly.

PART 3: Appreciate the use of four cardinal points in everyday life

What this means
In this part you learn to appreciate the use of four cardinal points in everyday life. You will use ideas from in your county, school, and Kenyan community.

How to learn it
1. Read the idea carefully: appreciate the use of four cardinal points in everyday life.
2. Locate, explain, then act responsibly using a Kenyan example from your life.
3. Check yourself: Can you explain it without looking?

Model
Participate: Describe one responsible action a Grade learner can take.

Your turn
Do one short practice that proves you can appreciate the use of four cardinal points in everyday life. Write or say your answer clearly.

PUT IT TOGETHER
Close your notes and say aloud: what Compass Direction is, one example, and one way you will practise this week.

SECTION 4: QUICK EXAMPLES

Good citizens follow rules, respect others, and care for shared places.

Kenyan examples: lining up, keeping the compound clean, telling the truth, helping a classmate.

Example 1: Connect “Compass Direction” to a real place or group in Kenya (school, market, county office, home). (skill: identify the four cardinal points of a compass)

Example 2: Give one cause and one effect linked to Compass Direction. (skill: use the four cardinal points to give directions on a map)

Example 3: Describe one responsible action a Grade learner can take. (skill: appreciate the use of four cardinal points in everyday life)

SECTION 5: PRACTICE NOW

1. Write 5 sentences (or show 5 clear steps) that teach Compass Direction to a classmate.
2. Practise this skill: identify the four cardinal points of a compass.
3. Practise this skill: use the four cardinal points to give directions on a map.
4. Practise this skill: appreciate the use of four cardinal points in everyday life.
5. Make one local Kenya example of Compass Direction from your county, market, farm, or school.
6. Mark your own work: What did you get right? What will you redo?

SECTION 6: WORK TO DO (HOME / REVISION)

1. In your exercise book, make a one-page revision sheet for Compass Direction: meaning, 3 examples, 5 practice items.
2. Teach a parent/guardian or younger sibling one part of this lesson (2 minutes).
3. Answer in writing: Why should a Grade 4 learner study Compass Direction?
4. Prepare for the quiz: cover the Remember box and recite it.

SECTION: THINK ABOUT IT

1. How can we show direction of places?

SECTION: REMEMBER

1. Know what Compass Direction means in your own words.
2. Use local Kenyan examples, not only definitions.
3. Practise in small steps, then check your work.
4. Be able to: identify the four cardinal points of a compass.
5. Be able to: use the four cardinal points to give directions on a map.

Now complete the Revision Quiz. Open Answers only after you finish.

— CBC Learn · Original study notes from KICD outcomes (Strategy 2)
